**Local AI. Limitless You.**

Lian+ downloads, runs and serves language and image models entirely on the phone.
No account, no API key, no inference server. It reads the hardware first and tells
you what the device can realistically run before you spend four gigabytes of mobile
data finding out.

## Install

Download `lian-plus-v0.1.0-arm64-v8a.apk` below and open it on the phone. Android
will ask you to allow installing from this source the first time.

- **arm64-v8a only** — that covers every modern phone.
- **Android 10 (API 29) or newer.**
- About 1.5 GB of free storage to be useful: the APK is 44 MB, but a first model
  is 1–5 GB on top.

The APK is signed with the standard Android debug key so it can be sideloaded.
That key is public, so treat this as a personal build rather than something to
distribute: for a signed release of your own, drop a `keystore.properties` in the
project root and run `./gradlew assembleRelease`.

```
SHA-256  9f93fc4cfa2a6158dc340c46d6d94ab093e2cf64ec48d6f747574bcbc38d592c
```

## First run

1. **Device** (Settings → This device) reads RAM, CPU cores and clocks, the Arm
   `dotprod`/`i8mm` extensions, GPU, storage and thermal state, then gives a
   verdict: which model sizes fit, how much context, how many threads and an
   estimated tokens/second.
2. **Models → Recommended** is filtered to that verdict. Pick one; downloads
   resume if the connection drops.
3. **Chat.**

On a 12 GB device (Galaxy S25 Ultra and similar) that means models up to 14B at
Q4, 16K of context, and 1024px image generation.

## What's in it

**Text** — llama.cpp, with prefix caching so a follow-up turn re-evaluates only
the new tokens, UTF-8 aware streaming that holds back the tail of a multi-byte
character until the bytes completing it arrive, and stop sequences matched on
decoded text rather than token boundaries.

**Context management** — the system prompt and the newest turns are pinned, older
turns are fitted into the remaining budget, and the overflow is compressed into a
running summary rather than dropped silently.

**Tools** — clock, calculator, device info, durable memory, document search, image
generation, and optional web search. Four tool-call syntaxes are parsed, because
local models are inconsistent about which they emit. Network tools are off by
default and cannot be switched on by a remote API caller.

**Retrieval** — import a text file and it is chunked on sentence boundaries,
embedded locally through a second small llama.cpp context, and searched by cosine
similarity before each reply.

**Images** — stable-diffusion.cpp with style presets and aspect ratios, running in
a separate OS process so its transient allocations cannot take the language model
down with them.

**Local API** — an OpenAI-compatible server on `127.0.0.1:8080` with streaming, so
any tool that speaks the OpenAI REST API can use the phone as its backend.

## Privacy

Conversations, documents and generated images stay in the app's private storage
and are never uploaded. Cloud backup is disabled. The app makes outbound requests
for exactly two things: model downloads from Hugging Face, and web search if you
turn it on.

## Known limits

- The engines have not been exercised on physical hardware yet — this build is
  verified to compile, pass its unit tests and package correctly, but on-device
  inference is untested. Please report what you hit.
- CPU inference only; the Vulkan and OpenCL backends are not enabled in this build.
- One generation at a time: concurrent API requests queue rather than interleave.
